skill.name: image-inpainting
skill.description: Mask-driven image inpainting on RunComfy through the runcomfy CLI. It routes masked edits to Z-Image Turbo Inpainting and suggests description-based edit models when no mask is available.
skill.summary: Run mask-based image inpainting jobs with RunComfy models from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, documentation links, placeholder URLs, or model-selection prose rather than executable Ruby or reconnaissance behavior. Confirmed risks are the intentional runcomfy command execution path, package-manager installation guidance, persistent API token storage, and an abuse risk around watermark removal.

remediation.suggestion: Keep the tool boundary limited to Bash(runcomfy *) and avoid expanding this skill to arbitrary shell, npm, or npx execution during normal use.
Document token revocation and cleanup steps, and verify that token files are created with owner-only permissions on all supported platforms.
Require user approval before sending private image URLs, masks, or prompts to RunComfy services.
Reframe watermark removal guidance to require ownership, authorization, or licensed cleanup use cases.

content.user_title: Repair Masked Image Regions with RunComfy
content.value_statement: Local image edits need clear model routing and mask-aware settings. This skill helps agents prepare RunComfy inpainting commands for object removal, region replacement, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Z-Image Turbo Inpainting for masked region edits.
Provides runcomfy CLI examples for object removal, background replacement, and description-based edits.
Documents required input fields such as source image URL, mask image URL, and prompt.
Suggests strength and control-scale ranges for cleanup, replacement, and full region changes.
Lists fallback models for edits where a precise binary mask is not available.
limitations: Requires a configured RunComfy account and runcomfy CLI for execution.
Requires source images and masks to be available as URLs accepted by the RunComfy API.
Does not create masks; users must provide masks from another tool.
Sends image references and prompts to an external RunComfy service.

use_cases.title: Clean Product Photos
use_cases.description: Remove distracting objects or replace a masked background while preserving the product area.

use_cases.title: Retouch Editorial Images
use_cases.description: Use low-strength inpainting to repair blemishes, gaps, or small unwanted regions in still images.

use_cases.title: Prototype Local Edits
use_cases.description: Compare mask-driven and description-based edit routes before choosing a model for production workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Remove a Small Object
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup with an existing mask.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-inpainting to remove the masked object from this image. Preserve the surrounding texture and lighting.

prompt_templates.title: Replace a Background
prompt_templates.prompt: Inpaint the masked background with a simple studio backdrop. Keep the subject, edges, shadows, and color balance unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Detailed Surface
prompt_templates.prompt: Fill the masked damaged area. Match nearby grain, perspective, color, and shadow. Do not change anything outside the mask.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a No-Mask Fallback
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced routing when only a text description identifies the region.
prompt_templates.prompt: No mask is available. Choose the best description-based RunComfy edit route and remove only the described region while preserving the rest.

output_examples.input: A street photo with a cable mask over the sky area.
output_examples.output: A RunComfy inpainting plan using Z-Image Turbo Inpainting, low strength, and preservation instructions for rooflines and sky tone.

output_examples.input: A product image with the full background masked.
output_examples.output: A high-strength replacement workflow that keeps the product unchanged and fills the background with neutral studio paper.

output_examples.input: A photo where no mask is available, but the unwanted mark is described by position.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to use a description-based edit model with a prompt that constrains changes to the specified area.

best_practices: Use masks that match the source image dimensions and cover only the intended region.
State what must remain unchanged outside the mask in every prompt.
Use lower strength for cleanup and higher strength for full replacement.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse a mask from a different image or layout.
Do not send private images to external services without user approval.
Do not use watermark removal unless the user owns the rights or has permission.

faq.question: Does this skill create masks?
faq.answer: No. It expects a source image URL and a mask image URL from another tool.

faq.question: Which model is the default route?
faq.answer: The skill recommends Z-Image Turbo Inpainting when a binary mask is available.

faq.question: Can it work without a mask?
faq.answer: Yes, but it switches to description-based edit models and loses precise mask control.

faq.question: What data leaves my environment?
faq.answer: The runcomfy CLI sends prompts and image references to RunComfy services for processing.

faq.question: Does it support video inpainting?
faq.answer: No. The skill points users to a separate video inpainting workflow.

faq.question: Can I control how much the masked area changes?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents strength ranges for cleanup, object replacement, and full region replacement.
